findings.reason: the repair must target the REFINED_FROM edge the census names, because removing a supersession pointer cannot zero cycles the detector finds on refine ancestry.
findings.text: `sib-lineage-cycle-repair` "breaks each cycle by removing one `HAS_SUCCESSOR` edge", but the evidence §52 inherits from `sib-lineage-cycle-census` reports the cycles on `REFINED_FROM`: its JSON summary records 68 `cycle_components` / 144 `cycle_names`, its `cycle_cross_check` query is `MATCH (n:StandardName) WHERE EXISTS { MATCH (n)-[:REFINED_FROM*1..]->(n) }` and agrees at 144, its limitations line reads "1859 of 1859 REFINED_FROM edges have empty property maps", its 86 `cases` carry `proposed_archive_edges` pointing into that REFINED_FROM edge list, and the proposed repair is "remove the listed edge(s) pointing from a superseded member onto this live identity". `HAS_SUCCESSOR` is the supersession pointer (§§16, 20, 21), not part of the refine-ancestry relation the cycles live in, so deleting one leaves every detected cycle intact: done-when bullet 3's "the live detector reports zero lineage cycles" is unreachable by the mechanism the section states, and the node would either report a false pass at a detector it re-fed against a different adjacency or strip 86 live supersession edges that no cycle required.

findings.reason: 86 live edge removals are scheduled against an adjudication the plan never declares, gates or cites, so the node blocks or writes without authority.
findings.text: `sib-lineage-cycle-repair` takes its per-cycle choice of edge "by a rule the census states", but the census states no rule: its `limitations` entry reads "Proposed repairs require lead adjudication", each of its 86 `cases` carries an English `proposed_repair` written for the lead to rule on, and §49's `sib-lineage-cycle-census` is declared read-only "with a disposable-graph reproduction where possible, at USD 0". §52 therefore schedules 86 live edge removals against an adjudication that has not been declared, cited or gated anywhere in the plan, and a worker holding this brief must either invent the selection rule or block.

findings.text: `sib-catalog-consistency` is measured only by "the after count is lower" against its own before-census, with no witness family and no negative control, so a run whose census loses sight of families scores as an improvement; the section's declared control (bullet 5, a source planted outside every class) is scoped to `sib-unaccepted-census` and does not reach this node.
